images.caption: A detailed anime-style character with silver hair and a yellow outfit is painted on the side of a maroon BNSF hopper, 491947. The piece stands out against the dark red paint of the car.

The green boxcar is fully in frame, showing a composed piece: white stencil text across the top, a large white 'N' logo, and a blue and white wildstyle lettering run with character work along the bottom. A grey boxcar follows at the right edge.
A multi-color wildstyle piece in pink, green, and blue with character work sits low along the panel of a maroon BNSF boxcar 492170, with the big white BNSF logo still reading above it.

A full pictorial mural of stylized orange and blue fish runs the length of the lower panels, an intentional picture-first piece on a white TTX auto-carrier, reporting marks 300084, with a yellow throw-up at the left end.
A composed piece featuring yellow lettering and a central character with a red face and blue outline sits on the side of a BNSF boxcar. The car is identified as BNSF 498156.

A low, sprawling multi-color piece of pastel and pink figures sits along the lower panel of a maroon COER 321078 boxcar, while a large white block-letter piece dominates the adjacent BNSF car to the right. The train runs past a calm, tree-lined water body under a flat overcast sky.

A TILX boxcar 550318 is covered in a large panda face with big black eyes and a colorful, patterned body, a composed pictorial piece that stands out. A BNSF hopper with a black tag is at the left edge.

A striking monochrome wildstyle piece with heavy flowing linework and a figure-like form dominates the maroon boxcar side. The piece is rendered in grayscale tones against the dark red car, giving it a clean, intentional look.

A cream ICER hopper (311702) carries a long low band of green and red lettering along the lower panel, with a white character or figure worked into the middle of the piece. It is sandwiched between two maroon BNSF hoppers.

A muted, multi-color piece of rounded letters and pale character shapes worked across the lower side of a brown boxcar, the only real paint in this pass. The car sits low in the frame behind a pile of lumber.
A tan boxcar carrying a large, multi-colored graffiti piece with illegible lettering on its lower half. The car is moving, causing motion blur that softens the edges of the artwork.

A yellow boxcar with a large white throw-up piece on its lower side. The car is lettered with a blue and red logo and sits on a track beside a lake with a forested shoreline and mountains in the distance.

The same white "SKLO" throw-up is visible on a dark tank car, now positioned on the left side of the frame as the train moves. It is a simple, single-color letter piece on a black tank car, passing in front of a calm lake and a distant, tree-lined shore under a flat, overcast sky.
A CN boxcar with a bold multi-color throw-up, the letters popping in red and white against the rust. The car is lettered CN and moving right.

A quick, single-color white throw-up reads "SKLO" on the side of a dark tank car, with a second smaller tag further right. It is a routine letter piece on a black tank car, passing in front of a calm lake and a distant, tree-lined shore under a flat, overcast sky.

A wildstyle piece in lime green and dark blue with character-like eyes and fill work covers the side of a maroon BNSF hopper, lettered 473912. The car rolls past a lake with a snow-capped peak on the horizon.

A white GATX boxcar (WRNX 40902) is the star of this pass, carrying a bold green and pink piece that reads like a stylized character or creature with sharp, interlocking linework and a small signature tag. The vibrant colors pop against the muted lake and overcast sky behind it.
A multi-colored piece with green, purple, and yellow lettering is on the side of a BNSF hopper. The piece is a bit smaller and less bold than the previous one, but still a solid piece of graffiti.
A painted portrait of a character is the focal point on this BNSF 498133 hopper, rendered in earthy tones against the maroon body. The piece is well-composed and centered on the visible side.

A composed piece fills the lower panel of a maroon BNSF hopper 474130: a green and blue cartoon character with a raised hand stands beside a large white-outlined 'EIADU' letterform, a clean, intentional composition. The car rolls past a wide river with a tree-lined far shore and a hazy snow-capped peak.

A composed piece on a CEFX 630914 boxcar pairs dark bubble letters with a central character figure, giving the dusty shell a real focal point. The car crosses the lakefront trestle with the forested far shore behind it.

A dark tank car carries a flowing white line-drawing of a winged figure or creature along its lower half, a composed pictorial piece that stands out on the black shell. The white XOMX car from the previous frame is now clipped at the right.

A cream-colored NOLX 852653 hopper carries a low, full-length pictorial piece of stylized characters and faces in muted yellow and brown tones, the image rather than letters doing the work. It is a composed, character-driven mural running along the bottom of the car.

A faded pictorial mural of a winged figure and a mountain range is painted in muted gray on the rust-colored side of a hopper, the image rather than lettering carrying the piece. The car sits center frame, flanked by a dark tank car and a white hopper.

A TILX boxcar 550318 is the real find: a large friendly panda face painted on the right end, paired with a blue-and-yellow wildstyle piece on the left. The character work is composed and intentional, making this a standout car on the train.
A composed character piece in teal, orange, and white with a stylized figure and abstract shapes is worked across the lower panel of a maroon BNSF hopper. A BNSF 479375 sits at the left edge.
A full-length piece of green and purple bubble letters with character work and stars fills the side of a COER hopper lettered 321045.

A bold, composed piece of thick white block letters on a dark background dominates the side of BNSF hopper 479369, with smaller white tags above. It is the strongest, most intentional work in the pass.
A BNSF hopper 478949 carries a yellow-outlined throw-up along the bottom with a small character figure worked in on the right. The bright yellow linework is the star of the car.

A yellow TTX boxcar carries a row of outlined blockbusters and small character tags along its lower panel, the most composed paint yet on the train. The TB OX car from the prior frame trails at the right.
